findings.evidence: The only scripted length stop is followed immediately by a successful answer. The gate never exercises consecutive stops through INCOMPLETE_RECOVERY_MAX_RETRIES=3, terminal cap handling, a delivered-turn/new-prompt counter reset, or the window-exhausted compaction path. This leaves named acceptance boundaries and the verification-gate contract's distinct fault checks unproven.

semanticReview.patch: The single-file candidate replaces the original inline developer reminder with a helper retaining the rendered text, role, content block, attribution and Date.now() timestamp. It awaits dropPersistedAssistantTurn before appending the same reminder object to agent state and SessionManager; subsequent replies follow it in both orders. No unrelated hunk or non-ASCII character was found.
semanticReview.retryAndCompaction: Code inspection: consecutive reasoning-only length stops take the below-threshold branch, increment the counter, drop each failed turn, and append one reminder when output usage is positive; the next stop at the cap durably drops its failed turn and blocks continuation. A delivered turn or new prompt resets the counter. Window-exhausted recovery runs compaction without invoking the new helper. These edge behaviors were inspected, not exercised by this review's gate.
semanticReview.otherAppends: session-maintenance.ts has only the new dual-write append. turn-recovery.ts:2862-2863 dual-writes reminders; 2878 plus appendCustomMessageEntry persists thinking-loop redirects. Its conditional assistant restoration at 1179-1187 writes nonempty turns to both; empty error turns can remain memory-only but convertToLlm drops ordinary error turns. agent-session.ts:1513-1514, 1524-1525, 8561-8562, 8611-8612 and 10006-10007 persist their appends; 3543's interrupted-thinking append is persisted at 3704-3711 when the same prompt generation survives. The known checkpoint-rewind reminder at 9843 and vibe-mode exceptions are out of scope. No other unpaired recovery reminder was found.
semanticReview.timestamp: For this developer reminder, stripping timestamp does not hide a field sent on the wire: Anthropic constructs message params from role/content (anthropic.ts:4914-5050), and Codex constructs input items from role/content (openai-codex-responses.ts:5403-5460). Timestamps can affect other preprocessing, but no inspected serializer transmits this reminder's timestamp as a message field. An unstripped check is possible for the reminder itself because the helper passes the same timestamped object to both append calls and SessionManager.open reads it back; compare its timestamp separately if retaining the normalized projection comparison.
